answer:
Growing rice on this field is severely limited, with a suitability score of 13 out of 100. The primary limiting factors are the soil pH and drainage conditions. 

Rice prefers acidic to neutral soils with an optimal pH of 5.5 to 7 [S1], whereas the SSURGO soil survey records an alkaline soil pH of 8.8. Furthermore, rice thrives in poorly drained conditions where fields remain saturated for more than half the year [S1], while the field's soil is well drained. 

While temperature (18.7 °C in the growing window) and texture (light, sandy loam) are tolerated, the high pH and well-drained soil make conventional rice production impractical here without major soil and water management interventions.
